When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs.  With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.
Job Title
Senior Optical Research Scientist/Engineer
Location(s)
High Wycombe
Job Description
Purpose
We are looking for an experienced optical scientist or engineer to lead the development, design and optimisation of advanced IR, UV and visible spectrometer systems. This role combines theoretical expertise with practical implementation in both research and commercial applications.
The successful candidate will develop a good understanding of the function and use of our products and their underlying technology, and will define and document both high-level functional and performance requirements and detailed sub-system requirements.
You will collaborate with key stakeholders to contribute to system design and specification, which may include concept development, design calculations or system modelling. The role includes collaboration with, and support of, PerkinElmer’s global R&D and manufacturing centres, which may involve travel.
The role also includes investigation of selected manufacturing and field failures on both new and existing products to determine root cause and initiate remedial actions.
You will have the opportunity to shape the optical design of next-generation spectroscopy instruments, working in a multidisciplinary team that covers everything from early research and new product development to sustaining existing products.
International and national travel may be required for conferences and trade shows, and to support PerkinElmer’s global R&D and manufacturing centres.
Responsibilities
Optical design and development
• Research, develop and implement optical system designs using principles of physical optics, radiometry and spectroscopy
• Drive the conceptual design and development of IR, UV and visible spectroscopic instruments
• Perform detailed optical modelling and analysis using advanced software tools (e.g. Zemax)
• Optimise and tolerance optical designs for performance and manufacturability
• Research and develop new spectroscopic techniques
• Understand and specify the products’ optical performance parameters at both system and sub-system level
Test, validation and data analysis
• Lead the validation and calibration of spectroscopic instruments
• Analyse experimental data and produce summary reports
• Work with other engineers to design and build the test equipment needed
Sustaining, product support and root cause analysis
• Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis for both new and existing products, covering development, manufacturing and field issues, working with design engineers, manufacturing and service to understand failure modes and quality issues
Collaboration and ways of working
• Collaborate with mechanical, electrical and systems engineers on integrated product design
• Author technical documentation, reports and research papers
• Work within our structured product development process
• Take responsibility for product quality and performance
Basic Qualification
Required:
• Degree (BSc or higher) in physics or an engineering discipline
• 5+ years’ experience in optical systems development
• Proven ability to design free-space coupled relay and imaging optical systems
• Well versed in the use of Zemax (or similar software) for ray tracing, analysis and optimisation
• Experience in the specification of optical components and knowledge of their manufacturing processes.
• Experience of planning and delivering work within a structured product development process
• Proven ability to assess technical risk and recognise failure modes
• Proven ability to design and carry out experiments, and to analyse and report on the results
• Proficiency in automated data collection and analysis using suitable software
Preferred Characteristics
• Postgraduate qualification (MSc or PhD) in an engineering or physical science discipline
• Experience designing reflective optical imaging or illumination systems
• Experience in the application of diffraction gratings for spectroscopy
• Knowledge of scanning Michelson interferometers
• Experience in the design, troubleshooting and manufacture of electro-mechanical equipment (preferably instrumentation)
• Product development experience within a company making measurement instrumentation
• Familiarity with product design methodologies such as design for manufacture (DFM) and design FMEATask- and goal-oriented, with the drive to see work through to completion
• Analytical thinker, driven by data
• Strong organisational skills
• Practical problem solver, comfortable switching between long-term development and urgent manufacturing issues
• Attention to detail
• Adaptable to change

Thanks to recent changes to our business units, we’ve gone back to first principles with our partnering function. Our business partners partner: that is their craft and their whole job. The deep specialist work in Reward, Talent, Learning and Development, and Employee Relations sits with our Centre of Excellence, and partners draw on that expertise rather than trying to do all of it themselves.
What that gives you is a role with focus. You get to know a part of the business properly, build relationships that mean something, and spend your time on the work that actually shifts performance. It also means you are never on your own, because you have specialists behind you.
This is the senior step on our partnering ladder for Tech, Product and Ops. You will hold the largest and most senior client group in the area, and you will lead a small team of two HR Business Partners, based in Kraków and Bangalore, who partner the layers of the business below you. You will be judged on the quality of your own partnering as much as on the strength and consistency of the team you lead.

• Lead, coach and develop your two HR Business Partners in Kraków and Bangalore, setting the standard for partnering across all three layers of the team and ensuring consistent quality wherever colleagues sit.
Lead organisation design and change

• Be accountable for the quality and consistency of ER practice across your area, and for making sure risk is surfaced early.
• Use what you see across cases to fix causes. Feed the patterns back so policy and manager capability improve.
Set the bar on culture and performance
• Own the engagement and culture agenda for a large or complex population, and hold leaders accountable for their own scores rather than carrying it for them.
• Set the standard for what good performance management looks like in your area. Push leaders to differentiate properly, recognise the best and act on the rest.
• Make sure your area’s strongest people are known, developed and kept, and that succession risk in critical roles is understood.
Make the wider People function better
• Shape how group and divisional programmes land across more than your own patch, and feed what you see on the ground back into the Centre of Excellence so that what they design works.
• Raise the bar in the team through mentoring, role modelling and improving how we partner. Be someone the more junior partners learn from, without needing a management title to do it.
• Work well across our locations, and help the team understand where local context should change our approach.
Bring insight, not just information
• Use people, cost and commercial data to bring your leaders insight they had not asked for.
• Build and defend a business case, in the language the business uses.
• Watch the external market and regulatory picture so you can see what is coming rather than react to it.
What does success look like?
• Your leadership team trusts you and involves you early.
• Change in your area is delivered on time, compliantly, and with colleagues understanding why.
• The hardest cases are handled well and quietly, and nothing significant surprises us.
• Engagement and performance in your area improve, and leaders are empowered to own that improvement themselves.
• Managers and more junior partners around you are visibly better because you are there.

Semtech’s High-Speed IC Design team is a highly experienced and collaborative engineering group developing industry-leading analog and mixed-signal solutions for next-generation optical communication systems.

These technologies are critical to enabling the continued growth of data centres, 5G infrastructure, and fibre-to-the-home networks.

The Analog Design Manager leads analog and mixed-signal design engineering activities across multiple high-speed IC product lines, owning the full new product introduction (NPI) lifecycle from product definition through to volume production.
The role is responsible for directing a multidisciplinary team of circuit designers and layout engineers, driving technical execution across concurrent development programmes, and ensuring robust delivery of high-performance IC designs aligned to business and customer requirements.
Responsibilities:
• Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team of analog circuit designers and layout engineers, including goal setting, performance management, recruitment, and capability development (20%).
• Own end-to-end NPI execution across multiple high-speed IC programmes, from concept and architecture through to tape-out, qualification, and production ramp (25%).

• Drive design execution across concurrent programmes, including scheduling, resource planning, and risk management (10%).
• Collaborate closely with Marketing, Product Definition, Applications, Product Engineering, Test, Validation, and Reliability teams to ensure full alignment with customer and system requirements (10%).
• Lead pre-tape-out reviews, ensuring design compliance against specification, layout verification, and production readiness (10%).
• Oversee post-silicon bring-up, silicon correlation, and performance optimisation to improve first-pass success rates and product maturity (10%).
• Prepare and present technical updates, design reviews, and programme status reporting to senior leadership, ensuring clear visibility of risks, milestones, and delivery progress (5%).
Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, or related technical discipline required
• 10+ years’ experience in semiconductor analog design required
• 5+ years’ experience in a leadership or engineering management role required
• Hands-on experience in analog circuit design, mixed-signal integration, simulation, and IC verification
• Proven experience leading NPI programmes within semiconductor development environments
• Strong ability to manage multiple concurrent projects under schedule and resource constraints
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across cross-functional engineering organisations
Desired Qualifications:
• Master’s degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering or related discipline preferred
• Experience in optical communication IC design, including laser drivers and transimpedance amplifiers
• Experience with SAP, semiconductor design tools, and advanced analog simulation environments

• Exposure to semiconductor device physics and analog design optimisation techniques
• Experience implementing engineering standards, methodologies, or design governance frameworks

Location: London Bridge Hospital
Contract: Permanent

At HCA Healthcare UK, we know that exceptional nurses are looking for more than just their next role. They want to work in an environment where advanced technology, clinical excellence and compassionate care come together. At The London Bridge Hospital, you’ll be part of a highly skilled team delivering some of the most complex and innovative procedures in cardiovascular, vascular and interventional care.
Rated “Outstanding” by the CQC, The London Bridge Hospital is one of the UK's leading private hospitals for complex cardiac care. Located in the heart of central London, just moments from London Bridge Station and on the banks of the River Thames, the hospital offers access to world renowned consultants, cutting edge technology and a truly multidisciplinary way of working. It is a place where you can continue to develop your expertise while helping patients receive outstanding care at every stage of their journey.
Joining our Cath Lab team means becoming part of a service that continues to invest in innovation. Our department includes three Cath Labs and supports a diverse and growing portfolio of procedures across cardiology, vascular, radiology and respiratory specialties.
You'll have the opportunity to work alongside leading consultants using advanced technologies, including the Ion robotic assisted bronchoscopy platform, which is helping transform the diagnosis of difficult to reach lung nodules and was first introduced to patients in Europe at The London Bridge Hospital. The technology enables greater precision and access during robotic assisted bronchoscopy procedures, supporting earlier diagnosis and enhanced patient care
Our Cath Lab service operates between 8am and 8pm, offering a range of flexible shift patterns to support both service needs and work life balance.
As a Staff Nurse in the Cath Lab, you'll play a vital role in delivering safe, high-quality care to patients undergoing diagnostic and interventional procedures. Working within a supportive multidisciplinary team, you'll provide expert clinical care before, during and after procedures while continuing to build your specialist knowledge across multiple areas of practice.
At HCA UK we care about what you care about. We care that you want to deliver the very best care. We care that you want a career you can be proud of. We care that you want working conditions that support your health and wellbeing. Let us care for you and your career, the same way you do for others.

• Work collaboratively with consultants and the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure outstanding patient outcomes.

• PICC line and Permcath insertions.
• Vascular procedures including EVAR.
• Advanced respiratory procedures including robotic assisted bronchoscopy using the Ion platform.

• Previous Cath Lab experience.
• Excellent communication and organisational skills.
• The ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
• A commitment to delivering safe, compassionate and patient focused care
Why HCA UK?
Originally founded over 50 years ago by Dr Thomas Frist, HCA has gone on to become one of the world’s leading healthcare providers. The Associate is expected to work with Senior Bankers in business origination and execution across Citi’s product set, with particular focus on episodic and strategic financing transactions. The overall objective of this role is to drive revenue by cross selling the Citi platform while efficiently deploying the firm's capital and evaluating and managing risk.
The role encompasses:
• Relationship management of the M&M portfolio comprised of the largest Metal producers and Miners in the world.
• This is an opportunity to join the team with heavy focus on global client set and delivery of market leading industry content, championing the deliverance of Corporate Finance initiatives.
• The Associate will be becoming an expert in the M&M space with exposure multiple relationship teams throughout Citi. They will also work very closely with our Investment Bank and product partners including Capital Markets (DCM, ECM, Acquisition & Project Finance, Leveraged Finance, etc.), Markets (Commodities, Derivatives, FX, etc.), Treasury & Trade Solutions (Trade Finance, Cash Management, etc.) and Corporate Finance / Lending initiatives.
• Providing analytical support, risk assessment and monitoring of existing and new relationships in the Industrials portfolio
• Developing good relationships with the clients and be viewed by clients as a specialist in the sector. The role involves a significant amount of direct client engagement at the CFO / Treasury level
Responsibilities:
• Partner with Senior Bankers to provide overall relationship management support for Global M&M clients along with industry support/expertise for the wider sector
• Member of deal team for the origination and execution of episodic and Corporate Finance transactions
• Responsible for staying abreast of market and industry trends, “best practices” and competitive landscape
• Risk assessment and credit analysis of existing relationships including periodic review of financial results and statements to monitor operating performance, liquidity position and financial condition, peer analysis, identifying industry trends and outlook and preparation of financial projections and sensitivity analysis
• Day-to-day responsibilities include developing client pitch materials tailored to meet client needs, lead execution of episodic transactions / financings and foster and leverage on-going relationships across the EMEA region
• Assist with day to day cash management activities, trading initiatives, foreign exchange, loan activity, debt and equity capital markets
• Responsible for evaluating public filings, research reports, operations, business plans, and financial forecasts to produce strategic and financial analyses
The associate will develop (i) in-depth understanding of the dynamics of the business, (ii) an understanding of clients’ priorities with the aim of identifying appropriate marketing opportunities and (iii) strong relationships internally with key product, risk and regional partners.
Qualifications & Skills:
• Strong experience working in a corporate bank, financing or a capital markets / investment banking role
• Prior experience in the Metals & Mining industry
• Corporate Finance mind-set with strong understanding of drivers of capital structure
• Strong credit skills, credit background and experience executing episodic transactions
• Quantitative, Accounting and Financial Modelling skills
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, notably Excel and PowerPoint
• Consistently demonstrates clear and concise written and verbal communication skills
• Bachelor’s/University degree or equivalent experience, MBA or Master's Degree in Business preferred
Competencies:
• Accounting & Corporate Finance
• Counterparty credit analysis and risk assessment
• Understanding legal documentation such as Loan Agreements and ISDAs
• Leadership in team-oriented environment
• Excellent interpersonal skills - able to create and sustain good personal contacts within the client group, balancing client requirements and Citi’s priorities
• Self-starter - prepared to take the initiative to follow issues through, whilst exercising judgment as to when to seek assistance
• Networking - maintaining close contact with product and risk specialists within Citi
Candidates applying for this role must be aware that it is a Certified Role, subject to the Certification Regime. The Certification Regime is one element of the Individual Accountability Regime which has come into effect on 7 March 2016. Under the Certification Regime, certain Citi entities must ensure that employees working in certain roles categorised as specified significant harm functions (Certified Roles) are assessed as fit and proper to carry out their role.
Under the guidance provided by the FCA and PRA, firms should have regard to the following when assessing fitness and propriety:
Honesty, integrity and reputation
Financial soundness
Competence and capability
In order to comply with the requirements of the Certification Regime, certain Citi entities must take reasonable care to ensure that an employee does not perform a Certified Role without first being certified as Fit and Proper. For this reason, you will be assessed for this role against the Fit and Proper requirements, as described above. This assessment will be carried out through extensive interviews, self-disclosures, permitted criminal record checks, reference checks, credit checks and other background checks. If hired for this role, you will also be required to complete an annual declaration regarding your Fitness and Propriety.
By submitting your application, you acknowledge that you have read the information above and that you are applying for a Certified Role. You also agree to Citi carrying out any additional screening required, including permitted criminal record checks, reference checks, credit checks and any other background checks.

We believe in better. And we make it happen.
Better content. Better products. And better careers.
Working in Tech, Product or Data at Sky is about building the next and the new. From broadband to broadcast, streaming to mobile, SkyQ to Sky Glass, we never stand still. We optimise and innovate.
We turn big ideas into the products, content and services millions of people love.
And we do it all right here at Sky.
The Core responsibility of the Playout Controller is to manage the transmission of ‘Live’ complex events, as well as to provide schedule management, output monitoring and first line recovery for any Sky hosted channels.
The management of ‘live’ complex events includes, for example: broadcasts where the break structure is variable, the duration of the event is unpredictable or where the timings of two subsequent events may overlap.
Schedule management includes the preparation, checking and updating of automation schedules delivered into the area to ensure discrepancies are identified before the output is affected. It also includes the alteration of “live” automation schedules due to changing editorial or commercial requirements. For both the preparation and management of the automation schedules, a high degree of attention to detail and adherence to agreed process is necessary to avoid potential impact to the channel output.
Through monitoring of the channel outputs the Controller is responsible for the scheduled content being delivered to the distribution platforms without defect or degradation. Direct “eyeball” monitoring of the channel output is supported and enhanced through the use of automated fault detection and alarming which the Controller must be fully capable of interpreting and interrogating.
In the case of any fault or deviation from the required output it is the Controller’s responsibility to minimise impact to the viewing public either through restoration of service or by fault management. Knowledge of the playout infrastructure and agreed best practices for recovery are essential in performing this function effectively.
The Controller is skilled in the management of both server-based content and “live” content including complex live events.
The Controller will also be responsible for effective training of others, contributing to the integration of new systems and services. The Controller will prioritise incidents and escalate effectively, taking financial, reputational and stakeholder concerns into account.
What you’ll do
•
Schedule Preparation - performing required manual and automated tasks on the playout schedules to identify potential errors and known faults and ensure readiness for broadcast
•
Live schedule management – editing of live automation schedule to alter content or timings as required
•
Live schedule monitoring – monitoring the output of channels to confirm and maintain fault-free playout
•
Regulatory Knowledge – knowledge of Ofcom regulations and Sky policies
•
Fault Identification – immediate identification of any loss or degradation of the channel outputs, as well as loss of encryption or PIN protection
•
Fault recovery – use of system resilience or schedule editing to recover from channel loss or degradation
•
Fault management – use of on-screen messages, voice-overs, or other messaging to keep customers informed when a fault is not immediately recoverable
•
Escalation – efficient communication to 2nd line support teams and operational management
•
Editorial Knowledge – knowledge of Sky’s programming and promotional strategies.
•
Logging & Reporting – accurately recording any faults, changes, or other deviations from the originally scheduled content
•
Information Management – accurately passing on information to colleagues or operational management to ensure channel continuity
•
Communication – concise and accurate verbal and written communication, professional and courteous at all times
•
Training – passing on knowledge and experience of workflows, systems and procedures as required. Structured training of others utilising established training materials as required
•
Support – Provides support to the Playout Specialist and Operational Lead functions as required
•
Complex Live Event Management – line-up, preparation and control of complex live events including negotiation with production teams when event durations are variable or overlapping
•
Gallery Free Production – making any necessary editorial decisions to maintain channel continuity when communication with event source is incoming only e.g. World Feed
What you’ll bring
•
Qualifications - degree qualification or relevant vocational qualifications
•
Specialist Knowledge – skilled in Playout systems and workflows, skilled in managing live events, skilled in Playout systems used by Sky, skilled in managing live Sports events
•
Industry Experience – Experience of digital playout environment, complex Live broadcast experience
•
Leadership Skills - Excellent communication & influencing skills, excellent decision making and prioritisation skills
The Sky Playout Team works 24/7 365 days a year to ensure that Sky Customers are receiving the best quality live sports and entertainment programmes. You’ll be joining the team and working a fixed shift pattern of day, mid and night shifts.

MoneySavingExpert.com (MSE) is the UK’s largest consumer website, providing free, independent and editorially led help to millions of people looking to save money. Our mission is simple: to help people cut their bills and achieve financial justice.
Around 12 million people visit MSE each month, while more than nine million subscribers receive our weekly email, packed with exclusive deals, tips, and guides.
What makes MSE distinctive is our Editorial Code, which underpins everything we do. Whatever your role, you will champion the consumer. If you are motivated by our mission and want to make a practical difference to people’s financial lives, MSE could be the right next step for you.

MSE’s Press Team helps ensure consumers across the UK can access MSE’s trusted personal-finance guidance. We generate more than 2,000 pieces of media coverage each month, using press activity to help people understand their rights, make informed financial decisions, and improve their financial wellbeing.
As Press Officer, you will support a busy press office across print, digital and broadcast media. You will help respond to the news agenda, develop proactive media opportunities, and amplify MSE’s editorial work, investigations, and campaigns.
This is an early-career role, suited to a recent graduate or someone in their second role who is looking to build hands-on experience in a high-profile national press office. Reporting to the PR Manager, you will be supported to develop your media judgment, writing, journalist relationships and understanding of consumer issues.
How you’ll spend your day:
·       Supporting the running of a busy, reactive press office by managing and responding to enquiries from print, digital, and broadcast media.
·       Drafting press releases, media lines and reactive comments in response to consumer issues in the news.
·       Monitoring the media landscape to identify proactive opportunities for MSE to provide comment.
·       Maintaining media distribution lists and building strong working relationships with journalists.
·       Supporting MSE’s 11 spokespeople, including Martin Lewis, to identify and prepare for relevant media opportunities, working with the PR Manager on high-profile or complex requests
·       Working closely with the News, Campaigns and Social teams to coordinate and amplify investigations, editorial content, and campaigning activity.
·       Keeping up to date with PR best practice, ethics and developments in the media landscape
What value you’ll bring to the role
·       A genuine interest in a career in public relations and the UK media landscape. You will likely read, watch, or listen to a broad range of news content each day.
·       Curiosity about the changing ways people discover news and information, including influencers, podcasts, digital-first broadcasters and other emerging media channels, and an interest in how MSE could use these to reach new audiences.
·       Enthusiasm for consumer issues and personal finance, and motivation to champion consumers
·       Strong written communication skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear, accurate and engaging copy.
·       Good judgement, attention to detail, and the ability to scrutinise information carefully before communicating it externally.
·       Confidence communicating with journalists, spokespeople and colleagues at all levels of the business.
·       An understanding of how PR can support wider campaigning, reputation, and brand objectives.
·       The ability to manage multiple tasks, work to tight deadlines and adapt calmly as priorities change.
·       A collaborative, can-do approach, with a willingness to learn, bring ideas and take ownership of your professional development.
We welcome applications from people with relevant experience gained through work, internships, volunteering, student journalism or similar. You do not need prior experience in personal finance or financial services; curiosity, sound judgement and a willingness to learn matter most.
Nice to have:
·       Knowledge of financial services or personal finance.
·       An understanding of Parliament, regulation and how policy is made.

The ERP Product Manager role exists to establish clear ownership of Apollo’s D365 F&O environment and turn it into a strategically managed business platform rather than a reactive support service. The role is accountable for ensuring the ERP environment remains stable, governed, prioritised and aligned to business objectives, while working closely with stakeholders across Apollo to identify opportunities for innovation, process improvement and operational efficiency. Over time, this role will be pivotal in shaping a scalable, well-controlled ERP platform that not only supports Apollo today, but also creates the foundation for future Apollo group companies to join the solution in a structured and sustainable way. In doing so, the role is intended to increase the value the business gets from D365, reduce inefficiency, strengthen internal ownership, and help Apollo operate more effectively as it grows.
Key Responsibilities
1. ERP Product Ownership
• Own the D365 F&O platform as a business product, ensuring clear accountability for roadmap, priorities, service performance and continuous improvement.
• Act as the primary internal owner of the ERP environment, ensuring the platform supports business operations effectively and evolves in a controlled, value-led way.
2. Governance, Demand and Prioritisation
• Own and operate the ERP governance cadence, including service reviews, change reviews, prioritisation forums and decision-making structures.
• Maintain a clear single front door for ERP business demand, ensuring requirements, issues, enhancements and optimisation ideas are triaged consistently and prioritised against business value, risk and capacity.
• Ensure ERP demand is translated into a managed, visible backlog with agreed priorities, ownership and delivery expectations.
3. Lifecycle, Releases and Environment Control
• Own the ERP release calendar and lifecycle approach, including readiness gates, go/no-go decisions, environment discipline and release governance.
• Ensure product updates, configuration changes, improvements and platform changes are planned, communicated and delivered in a controlled way.
• Work with business SMEs, internal IT and external partners to ensure release readiness, testing discipline and deployment confidence.
4. Partner and Supplier Management
• Own the operational relationship with D365 managed service, support and delivery partners.
• Manage partner performance, escalation, service reporting and commercial discipline to ensure delivery aligns with business objectives and agreed standards.
• Maintain clear boundaries between BAU support, project delivery, optimisation work and hypercare to avoid unmanaged ownership gaps.
5. Continuous Improvement and Optimisation
• Proactively identify opportunities to improve the ERP platform, simplify processes, reduce friction and increase business value.
• Work with business stakeholders to shape and prioritise optimisations, ensuring improvements are aligned to the wider business roadmap and platform standards.
• Own the ERP improvement backlog and ensure incremental change is driven purposefully rather than reactively.
6. Product Roadmap and Business Alignment
• Define and maintain the ERP roadmap, balancing operational stability, technical debt, mandatory updates, risk reduction and business-led change.
• Ensure the business understands what is planned, why it is prioritised and what value it is expected to deliver.
• Act as the bridge between business process needs and ERP platform direction.
7. Standards, Controls and Platform Guardrails
• Define and maintain ERP standards covering platform usage, integrations, controls, change discipline, documentation and configuration governance.
• Ensure appropriate controls and guardrails exist around access, change, environment use and platform decision-making.
• Protect the integrity of the ERP environment by ensuring changes are consistent with agreed standards and architecture principles.
8. Documentation and Platform Knowledge
• Ensure ERP platform documentation remains current, structured and useful, including configurations, procedures, key decisions, environment information and operating guidance.
• Strengthen internal ownership and knowledge retention so the environment is less dependent on third parties over time.
9. Stakeholder Management
• Build effective working relationships across Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Warehouse, Quality, Engineering and IT stakeholders.
• Translate technical or platform constraints into sensible business decisions and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Act as the accountable point of contact for ERP platform decisions, priorities and issues.
Scope Boundaries
In Scope
• D365 Finance & Operations platform ownership.
• ERP governance, prioritisation, roadmap, lifecycle and release management.
• Managed partner and support partner accountability.
• Continuous improvement, optimisation intake and business-driven enhancement prioritisation.
Out of Scope
• Hands-on development build work as a primary responsibility.
• Power BI platform ownership / BI delivery management.
• CRM/CE product ownership and business ownership.
Skills & Experience
Essential
• Strong experience with Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations in a live, business-critical environment.
• Proven experience in ERP service ownership, application/product ownership, ERP management, or a similar senior techno-functional platform role.
• Strong understanding of ERP governance, prioritisation, lifecycle management and controlled change.

Clean Water and Wastewater Networks • Northumbrian Water
DEPARTMENT / FUNCTION Operations / Networks Delivery REPORTS TO Team Leader / Site Supervisor LOCATION Northumbrian Water operating region (North East England)
CONTRACT
Permanent • Full time HOURS 50 hours • Mon–Fri CLIENT Northumbrian Water Group (NWG)
Purpose of the role
To carry out safe, high-quality excavation, installation, repair, reinstatement and associated groundworks on Northumbrian Water clean water and wastewater assets. Working as part of a civils crew under the Team Leader, the Operative delivers planned and reactive work to Northumbrian Water specifications, street works legislation, hygiene requirements and company SHEQ procedures.
Context
Northumbrian Water supplies water and wastewater services across the North East of England. Delivery includes planned capital and maintenance work and reactive repair, often in live highways, private land and operational sites. The Civils Operative is a hands-on member of the crew, responsible for the quality of their own work, safe working around buried services, and a professional standard with customers and the public.
Key accountabilities
Civils and network operations
• Carry out excavation, trench support, pipe laying, jointing, connections, repairs and backfill on water mains, services, sewers, rising mains, chambers, manholes and associated assets.
• Install, repair and replace ironwork, covers and frames, chambers, ducting and minor civil structures to specification.
• Undertake highway and private-land reinstatement, including bituminous, concrete, flagged and landscaped finishes.
• Support mains isolations, commissioning, chlorination and hygiene arrangements in line with the Disinfection Code of Practice and clean-water protocols.
• Operate plant and equipment within competence and permit conditions, including excavator and dumper where ticketed, compaction plant and hand tools.
• Use abrasive wheels, cutting and grinding equipment only when trained and authorised.
• Locate and avoid buried services using safe digging practice and HSG47 principles, including CAT and Genny where trained.
• Identify and report defects, uncharted apparatus and network risks to the Team Leader.
• Respond to reactive and emergency work, including bursts, collapses, flooding, dangerous apparatus and out-of-hours call-out when on rota.
Health, safety, environment and quality
• Work to the safe system of work, risk assessment, method statement and permits briefed by the Team Leader.
• Help set out and maintain barriers, signing, lighting and guarding in accordance with NRSWA / Safety at Street Works and Road Works.
• Work safely in excavations and, where trained, support confined-space activities under a written safe system of work.
• Use correct manual handling techniques and mechanical aids; do not lift beyond capability.
• Protect live services, the environment and water quality; control silt, fuel, spoil and waste.
• Stop work and report immediately if conditions are unsafe, a service is struck, or a near miss occurs.
• Leave a clean, secure and compliant site at the end of each shift.
Customer and records
• Represent the company and Northumbrian Water professionally on customers’ property, in the highway and on operational sites.
• Complete personal timesheets and support site records, photographs and materials returns as directed.
• Follow instructions from the Team Leader and raise issues early if the job cannot be completed as planned.
Essential requirements
• Experience as a civils, utilities or groundworks operative, ideally on water, drainage or highway works.
• Ability to work safely as part of a small crew on live sites and in public areas.
• Valid CSCS card (or equivalent).
• Full UK driving licence; ability to travel across the Northumbrian Water region and attend standby / emergency call-out.
• Physically fit for manual work and prepared to work outdoors in all weather.
• Reliable, safety-focused and willing to work flexible hours including early starts, weekends and a standby rota.
Desirable tickets and qualifications
• NRSWA / Street Works (Operative or Supervisor as appropriate to the role)
• Confined space (City & Guilds or equivalent)
• Excavator ticket (CPCS / NPORS or equivalent)
• Dumper ticket (CPCS / NPORS or equivalent)
• Manual handling
• Abrasive wheels
• First aid
• HSG47 – Avoiding danger from underground services (CAT and Genny / service avoidance)
• EUSR National Water Hygiene / Blue Card and SHEA Water.
• Experience on Northumbrian Water or another UK water company network.
Behaviours and competencies
• Puts health, safety and water quality first and will speak up if something is wrong.
• Takes pride in workmanship and leaves sites tidy.
• Works well in a team and follows briefings without cutting corners.
• Calm and polite with customers, even on reactive or disruption-related jobs.
• Willing to learn Northumbrian Water specifications, hygiene rules and new tickets.
Working environment
The role is predominantly outdoor and physically demanding. Work takes place in live highways, excavations, operational treatment and network sites, and private property, in all weather. The post holder must be fit for manual work, prepared to work in muddy, confined or hygienically controlled conditions, and able to wear required PPE including hygiene clothing on clean-water tasks.
Additional information
A full occupational driving assessment, drugs and alcohol screening, and baseline health surveillance may be required. Training will be provided on Northumbrian Water systems, specifications and hygiene protocols where these are not already held. The employer reserves the right to amend duties in line with operational need across AMP programmes and reactive networks contracts.

As a Senior Competitor Analyst at Nexperia, you will play a critical role in strengthening our competitive position within the power semiconductor market. You’ll lead the physical and electrical analysis of competitor MOSFET technologies, generate high‑value benchmarking insights, and support strategic decision‑making across Product Development, Marketing, Technology Roadmapping, and wider business planning.
This is a highly collaborative, technically demanding role where your expertise in Failure Analysis techniques and data analytics will directly influence our product portfolio, cost models, and long‑term technology direction.
What you will do
As a Senior Competitor Analyst, you will be responsible for delivering high‑quality competitor intelligence and cost / performance benchmarking outputs. Your key responsibilities include:
• Performing detailed physical analysis ‘teardown’ of competitor MOSFET devices to package and wafer level using Failure Analysis techniques (FIB, SEM, X‑ray)
• Coordinating electrical performance benchmarking of competitor products versus Nexperia devices
• Providing cost estimates of competitor products and technologies
• Developing, calibrating, and refining cost models
• Delivering technical data and analytical insights to R&D and Marketing
• Monitoring MOSFET technology trends and competitor activity
• Overseeing the physical analysis pipeline, including 3rd‑party labs
• Conducting benchmark reviews and contributing to DeepDive sessions
• Driving improvement activities within the benchmarking function
What you will deliver
• High‑quality competitor teardown and cost / performance benchmarking reports
• Accurate cost models
• Quarterly competitor updates
• DeepDive input and technology insights
• Improved throughput and efficiency of the physical analysis pipeline
• Analytical insights that influence technology developments, product portfolios and strategic direction
What you will need
Essential requirements
• Degree in Electrical / Electrical Engineering, Semiconductor Physics, or related discipline
• Several years’ experience in the semiconductor industry, or similar
• Advanced knowledge & skills on Failure Analysis techniques (FIB, SEM, X‑ray)
• Proficient understanding of semiconductor devices, process flows and manufacturing
• Advanced level in statistical methods, modelling, and database management
• Experience in creating analysis reports, dashboards, and data visualisation (Excel, PowerBI)
• Excellent communication skills, able to present to peers and senior stakeholders
• Strong collaborator, able to engage and discuss ideas with stakeholders
Beneficial
• Coding skills (eg Python)
• Understanding of the power semiconductor business, it’s technologies and portfolios
Interview process
• Stage 1: Recruiter Review
• Stage 2: 60‑minute Technical Interview
• Stage 3: 60‑minute Competency Interview
Your benefits will include
Remuneration & Reward – Excellent starting salary, bonus up to 6%, excellent contributory pension scheme of up to 9%, recognition rewards scheme, EV salary sacrifice scheme, income protection, and 12× salary life assurance policy.
Health & Wellbeing – 33 days annual leave, hybrid and flexible working, flexible benefits scheme, enhanced parental leave, on‑site medical centre, enhanced sick pay, subsidised canteen, employee assistance programme, retail and entertainment discounts, a variety of sports and social clubs.
Professional Development – Possibility for funded academic support up to PhD level, employee goal setting and development plans, huge growth potential both internally and globally within the business via both management and technical pathways.
Corporate Social Responsibility & Sustainability – A global commitment to becoming carbon neutral by 2035, working with suppliers who embrace and comply with the Nexperia Supplier Code of Conduct, paid time off for every employee to support charitable work up to four times per year.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion – Corporate members of Neurodiversity in Business and a Disability Confident Employer. Dedicated Employee Resource Groups for Neuroinclusion, the LGBTQ+ community, and Women in Nexperia, with a commitment to increase women in management positions to 30% by 2030.
Talent acquisition based on Nexperia vacancies is not appreciated. Nexperia job adverts are Nexperia copyright © material and the word Nexperia® is a registered trademark.
D&I Statement
As an equal-opportunity employer, Nexperia values diversity not just because it is the right thing to do but because diverse teams perform better. We are dedicated to being inclusive, and a proof point of this dedication is that we were the main partner of the very first Dutch Paralympic Team NL House during the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games. Our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible to all, and we consider all applicants fairly, as well as providing a safe work environment and reasonable adjustments where requested.
In addition, we offer our colleagues the possibility to join employee resource groups such as the Pride Network Group or global and local Women's groups. Nexperia is committed to increasing women in management positions to 30% by 2030.

Donaldson is committed to solving the world’s most complex filtration challenges. Together, we make cool things. As an established technology and innovation leader, we are continuously evolving to meet the filtration needs of our changing world. This group is responsible for step change product developments, ensuring product underpins the strategy of innovative solutions to complex industrial filtration challenges.

The role plays a key part in driving efficiency, continuous improvement and effective teamwork, contributing to business performance and providing a positive experience for customers and stakeholders
Role Responsibilities:
• Design complete commercially viable electrical systems for in development Donalson Bofa Fume extraction products
• Develop and optimise electrical designs for historic products with a focus on operational or legislative improvements (cost down, production build, component selection and availability, compliance)
• Ensure all electrical designs comply with relevant regional and international machinery safety and electrical design standards (e.g., UL 508A, IEC 60204-1, and CE requirements).
• Design and validate systems compliant with hazardous area regulations (e.g., ATEX, UKEX, NFPA 652/484) for applications involving combustible dusts or volatile chemical vapours
• Produce and maintain accurate electrical schematics and Bills of Materials BoMs in readiness for procurement and manufacturing
• Collaborate with project management to establish and align realistic project timelines and deliver on the committed schedule
• Work with mechanical, electronics and software engineers to integrate designs within overall system architecture
• Support all activities leading to successful on-going sale of product and new development including escalations in technical support, prototype build and test
• Provide technical expertise and guidance on industrial power distribution, EMC design principals, cable sizing and protection, electrical testing and system validation
• Support continuous improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing product performance, quality, safety, reliability and manufacturing efficiency
Minimum Qualifications:
• Formal electrical qualifications (Electrical engineering, electrical & electronic engineering, Control systems engineering or a related discipline)
• 5+ years industrial experience designing electrical systems or control panels
• Strong understanding of electrical design standards and regulatory requirements
Preferred Qualifications:
• Proficiency in electrical drafting software (e.g., AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN, Altium Harness).
• Experience using SolidWorks or equivalent 3D CAD software
• Strong understanding of product development processes and systems engineering
• Experience working within a manufacturing or industrial engineering environment.
• Knowledge of hazardous area design requirements, including ATEX and UKEX compliance.
• Experience supporting products through the full lifecycle, from concept through to manufacture and field support

About the Role
The Senior Quantity Surveyor supports construction project delivery by monitoring progress through the measurement and evaluation of installed quantities against approved plans and baselines. The role integrates quantity tracking, forecasting, and estimate loading with cost and performance metrics, contributing to value engineering, cost-benefit analysis, and feasibility assessments across labour, materials, and execution strategies. Working under general direction, the position applies specialised project controls knowledge to interpret complex issues, maintain accurate MTO data from IFC drawings, and support informed decision-making. The role also provides guidance to less experienced team members while ensuring delivery is aligned with organisational policies, procedures, and business objectives.

•
Monitor construction progress through detailed measurement and evaluation of installed quantities against approved plans and baseline estimates
•
Maintain and update quantity take-offs and material take-offs (MTOs) based on Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings to support accurate progress tracking
•
Develop and maintain forecasting models, including estimate loading and cost projections aligned with project schedules and delivery milestones
•
Perform cost-benefit analysis, value engineering assessments, and feasibility studies to optimise labour, materials, and execution strategies
•
Analyse variances between planned and actual quantities and provide insights to support corrective actions and commercial decisions

Contribute to project controls reporting by integrating quantity, cost, and progress data into standard reporting deliverables

Support compliance with company policies, procedures, and project governance frameworks in all quantity surveying activities

Proven experience with quantity tracking, measurement, and progress reporting on large-scale projects
•
Experience developing forecasts, cost estimates, and project controls reporting
•
Experience interpreting and working from Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings

Experience in value engineering and cost analysis within project delivery environments
Desirable

About Ofcom
As the UK’s communications regulator, we’re delivering vital work that helps keep the UK connected and shapes the future of how we’ll stay connected with each other.
Our work covers everything from phones and broadband, through to TV, radio, the postal service, and wireless devices. We’re also taking on the challenge of making the online world a safer place. And we need people of all backgrounds, skill sets, and experiences to help us achieve our goal of making communications work for everyone.
About the Team
The Online Safety Group’s purpose is to ensure UK citizens have a safer life online by implementing and overseeing the requirements under the Online Safety Act 2023. The Group is responsible for delivering online safety policy, supervising online services, and building technical expertise to meet the regime’s aims.
This role is within the Online Safety Policy Development team, which works at the centre of the Online Safety Group. The Policy Development team lead the development of Ofcom’s online safety policies which establish steps services should take to make users safer online. They are policy experts in online harms, mitigations and are responsible for implementing our policy codes and guidance.

This could include policy development, implementation, compliance initiatives, and other cross-cutting work needed to deliver the online safety regime effectively.
Current priority areas include, but are not limited to, Women and Girls' Online Safety, Age Assurance, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the proposed social media ban.

• Uses professional/operational knowledge and expertise to deliver priorities they are accountable for on time, and to a high standard
• Support project teams to solve complex policy problems by developing options and considering their practicality, risks and long-term implications.
• Research and analyse multiple data sources on particular topics and draw conclusions together for the wider team.
• Ensure the delivery of clear, concise and focused documents, such as meeting notes, agendas, briefings, consultation documents and research reports, for internal use or external publication.
• Provide practical project management support to work areas, such as setting up meetings, project planning and feeding into programme management.
• Support your team to build and maintain strong relationships with relevant online services in order to understand, assess and, where necessary, support improvements in protections for users.
• Develop and foster online expertise across Ofcom’s online work programme and keep across online trends and technological developments. Keep abreast of the public policy landscape in relation to online regulation.
Please note, this role may involve some research or policy development into areas such as preventing hate and terrorism, online child sexual abuse, material promoting suicide or self-harm, or other potentially sensitive and/or distressing topics.

Senior Medical Writer
ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.
As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.
As a global provider of drug development solutions, our work is serious business. But that doesn’t mean you can’t have fun while you do it. With our vision to be the partner of choice in drug development, we hire only the best and brightest in the industry. Are you one of them?
We are looking for conscientious, resilient, and inspiring individuals to join our team. As a Senior Medical Writer (SMW), your primary responsibility will be to provide scientific and medical/clinical writing support as part of a dedicated team servicing an assigned client. While the ability to work independently is key, the SMW will work closely with the Scientific Manager (ie, Scientific Director) and other members of the client account team to help ensure the timely delivery of high-quality and scientifically/medically accurate assigned projects. As a Senior Medical Writer, your review of junior writers’ work will also be a key part of this role. Your participation in internal company initiatives, as required, offers additional potential opportunities for growth.
The Role
As a Senior Medical Writer (SMW), prior in-depth experience with background researching, developing, and writing for the diverse array of deliverables within medical publications and medical communications is expected and will be an integral foundation for this role. The SMW role will fall broadly across the following approximate allocations (individual client account teams may have, from time to time, specific needs that may alter these allocations as may be necessary/required).
The vast majority of your time will be devoted to content development and writing, from inception to delivery, including but not limited to:
• responsibility for the accurate interpretation of clinical data (e.g., from clinical study reports, safety summaries, biostatistical tables, published articles, etc), and its accurate, concise adaptation to meet assigned projects’ stated objectives
• all compliance requirements for medical publications and medical communications, as relevant and appropriate (e.g., authorship guidelines, journal requirements, client confidential materials, etc)
• representing assigned work at internal and external (client) meetings as required (e.g., project status, author interactions, client publication committee meetings, etc)
• understanding and contributing to client publication and communication plans as required (e.g., impact on project timelines, appropriate congress and journal venues for assigned client/therapy area, relevance to client drug development planning, etc)
Some of your time will provide an opportunity to assist in the management of medical writing resources, including but not limited to, responsibility for:
• monitoring and helping to manage the medical writing workload, including for junior/other writers, as required
• collaboration with the Scientific Manager (ie, Scientific Director) and account managers to help ensure adherence to agreed-upon timelines (e.g., project status reports, proactive flagging of problems, resource limitations/availability, etc)
• assisting in the onboarding and mentoring of new and junior medical writers, as required
There may be on occasion opportunity to assist the SM (SD) and/or GMC Senior Leadership in business development activities such as background research and writing support for new business proposals
What you need
• Advanced degree, preferably PhD but PharmD and MD may also be considered
• Prior relevant experience in a medical publications/medical communications agency preferred
• Minimum of 3-5 years’ experience of high-level content development; applicants with 1-2 years’ experience as a Senior Medical Writer while at a medical communications agency preferred
• Proven history of relevant high-level writing support, including: proficiency with ICMJE and GPP guidelines; ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journal content; ability to develop and write to prescribed styles and formats
• Ability to work efficiently with network directories/databases
• Familiarity and ability to work with industry standard resources (e.g., PubMed/Medline, clinicaltrials.gov, various market intelligence/data analytic providers, etc)
• Ability to work with cross-functional teams (e.g., editorial/library services, graphics/digital services, presentations support, etc)
• Proficiency with commonly used software including but not limited to word processing (e.g., MS Word), graphics (e.g., PowerPoint or Prism), and bibliographic software (e.g., EndNote), and adaptability to other applicable software as may be required from time to time
• Experience in resource organizing and mentoring strongly preferred
• Must have demonstrable command of the English language (read, write and speak)
• A strong desire to be a key part of a global network of services that lead to better outcomes for its clients, its people and for patients…apply now and Own IT@ICON !
Employment with ICON is contingent upon having the legal right to work in the country where the role is based.
Rewards & Benefits
ICON offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your health, wellbeing, and career development.
Benefits may include:
• Competitive base salary and performance related incentives
• Health and wellbeing programmes including medical, dental, and vision coverage where applicable
• Retirement and pension plans
• Life assurance and disability coverage
• Employee assistance programmes and wellbeing resources
• Learning and development opportunities through structured training and career pathways
Benefits may vary depending on role and location.

Linklaters is a global law firm, providing legal services in 20 countries and through 30 offices.

Performance Management and Service Assurance
• Support the Technology Service Owners in establishing and maintaining performance baselines, service levels, KPIs and consistent reporting methods.
• Collaborates with the Technology Service Owners in the tracking of performance against contractual commitments, milestones, deliverables, SLAs and KPIs; identify adverse trends and provide concise updates to stakeholders.

Contract management and compliance

Lloyd’s is the world’s leading insurance and reinsurance marketplace, bringing together the world’s leading risk takers to advance global progress.
Our strategy is focused on delivering strong underwriting performance, operating an efficient and flexible marketplace, and maximising the capital advantage of the Lloyd’s market — while continuing to build a Lloyd’s we are proud of.
How we deliver this, matters. We take the risk, make things happen, and own the outcome — working together across our global network to turn insight into impact.
We’re looking for a Head of Claims Oversight to lead how we oversee, challenge and strengthen claims performance across the Lloyd’s market.
This is a senior, influential role with the opportunity to shape how claims is viewed, managed and continuously improved across the market. You’ll bring insight, judgement and a clear focus on outcomes. You’ll build trusted relationships with senior market leaders, use data to identify emerging risks and know when to challenge, intervene or escalate.
And you’ll lead a team with the expertise and confidence to make a difference.
What you’ll be doing
You’ll lead our Claims Oversight team and help ensure managing agents deliver claims services that meet Lloyd’s expectations and support strong syndicate performance.
You’ll:
• Lead Principle 4, Claims Management, within our Principles Based Oversight framework.
• Identify and respond to emerging claims performance risks, taking proportionate action when needed.
• Use claims data and management information to turn insight into focused market action.
• Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across managing agents, brokers and market representative groups.
• Lead our day-to-day relationship with the LMA on claims matters.
• Lead the claims response for Lloyd’s Major Event Response activity.
• Work closely with Claims Operations, Claims Insight, Underwriting, Pricing, Reserving, Customer and Culture teams.
• Influence the development of Lloyd’s claims and performance management strategy.
• Lead, develop and empower a high-performing Claims Oversight team.
This is about more than identifying problems. You’ll help shape better outcomes for the market.
What you’ll bring
We’re looking for someone with strong claims expertise, sound judgement and the ability to influence at senior level.
You’ll bring:
• Significant claims experience gained in an operational, technical or oversight environment.
• Strong knowledge of claims management and risk, alongside experience of the insurance or wider financial services sector.
• An understanding of Lloyd’s, the London Market and international insurance markets.
• Experience working with senior stakeholders in complex organisations and navigating competing priorities.
• Evidence of influencing and negotiating challenging issues to reach effective outcomes.
• Experience leading and developing teams or subject matter experts.
• The ability to interpret complex information and turn it into clear, concise recommendations.
• Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills, with evidence of taking ownership through to delivery.
• Experience delivering business change or improvement.
You don’t need to approach every challenge in the same way. We value leaders who listen, adapt and bring different perspectives together to get to the right outcome.
The opportunity
Claims matters. It’s where the promise made through insurance becomes real.
In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to influence claims performance across the Lloyd’s market while helping us respond to major events and emerging risks.
You’ll challenge constructively. You’ll use evidence to focus attention where it matters. And you’ll give your team the confidence and space to use their expertise.
Our strategy is focused on strong underwriting performance, an efficient and flexible marketplace, and maximising the capital advantage of the Lloyd’s market.
Being inclusive at Lloyd’s is integral to how we work — and how we deliver impact.
We aim to build a diverse, inclusive environment that reflects the global markets we serve, where everyone is treated with dignity and respect and supported to reach their full potential.
We take the risk by challenging traditional thinking and being proactive about inclusion. That means being open and positive about workplace adjustments, prioritising health and wellbeing, and investing in diversity and inclusion training so everyone feels able to contribute and succeed.
We make things happen by turning our commitment into action. Through employee networks, mentoring, volunteering opportunities and sustained investment in professional development, we create an environment where inclusion is experienced day‑to‑day — not just talked about.
We own the outcome by focusing on impact. By bringing together diverse perspectives and the best minds in the industry, we work collaboratively with underwriters and brokers to create innovative, responsive solutions that share risk and solve complex problems across global markets.
